what do mathematicians call any rectangu: In mathematics, a matrix is a rectangular array of numbers, symbols, or expressions arranged in rows and columns, widely used to solve systems of linear equations.
what do pandas mostly eat?: Bamboo makes up about 99% of a giant panda's daily diet. Because bamboo provides little nutrition, an adult panda can spend up to 12 hours a day eating and consume roughly 26 to 84 pounds (12 to 38 kg) of it daily.
what do people often hunt for at easter?: Easter egg hunts are a traditional springtime activity where children search for hidden dyed hard-boiled eggs or chocolate eggs, which symbolize new life and resurrection.
what do plants need from the sun to make: During photosynthesis, plant cells use green chlorophyll pigments to absorb sunlight, converting water and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen.

what do scientists call dinosaur bones f: Fossils are the preserved remains, impressions, or traces of organisms from past geological ages, typically formed when bone mineralizes in sedimentary rock over millions of years.

what do the rings on a tree tell us?: Dendrochronology is the science of dating trees by counting annual growth rings, which form as a tree adds light-colored wood in spring and denser, darker wood in late summer.

what do we call a storage place for bees: An apiary comes from the Latin word apis, meaning bee, and refers to a collection of beehives. An aviary, derived from avis, is a large enclosure for keeping birds.
what do we call a triangle that has thre: A scalene triangle has three sides of completely different lengths and three unequal angles. In contrast, an equilateral triangle has three equal sides, and an isosceles triangle has two.
what do we call an angle of less than 90: An acute angle measures between 0 and 90 degrees. An obtuse angle measures greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees, while a reflex angle exceeds 180 degrees.
what do we call the longest day of the y: The summer solstice occurs when a hemisphere is tilted closest to the Sun, producing the longest day and shortest night of the year around June 21 in the north and December 21 in the south.
what do we call the moon when it looks l: A full moon occurs when the Moon sits opposite the Sun relative to Earth, completely illuminating the side facing us. A new moon occurs when the illuminated side faces entirely away.
what do we call the square root of negat: The symbol i represents the imaginary unit, defined such that i squared equals -1. Mathematician Leonhard Euler introduced this notation in 1777.
what do we call these numbers: 0, 1, 4,: Square numbers are formed by multiplying an integer by itself, such as 0x0=0, 1x1=1, 2x2=4, and so on. Cubic numbers involve multiplying an integer by itself twice, yielding values like 1, 8, and 27.

which continent is egypt in?: Egypt is primarily located in northeastern Africa, though its Sinai Peninsula extends across the Suez Canal into Western Asia, making it a transcontinental nation.
which continent is the island of madagas: Madagascar sits in the southwestern Indian Ocean about 250 miles (400 km) off the coast of Mozambique, making it geographically part of the African continent.
which continent is the sahara desert loc: The Sahara covers roughly 3.5 million square miles (9 million square km) across North Africa, making it the largest hot desert on Earth.

which country is divided by a canal conn: The Panama Canal opened in 1914, cutting roughly 50 miles (80 km) across the Isthmus of Panama to link the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. It eliminated the need for ships to navigate the hazardous route around South America's Cape Horn.

which greek god was the god of the sun?: Helios was the Titan god and personification of the Sun, driving a fiery four-horse chariot across the sky each day, though Apollo was also later conflated with the sun in classical literature.
which greek god/goddess tossed a golden: Eris, the goddess of discord, threw the golden apple after being excluded from the wedding of Peleus and Thetis. The resulting dispute among Hera, Athena, and Aphrodite sparked the Judgement of Paris and ultimately the Trojan War.

which hebrew phrase is most commonly ass: Mazel tov translates literally from Hebrew to 'good constellation' or good fortune, and is widely used to celebrate weddings, bar mitzvahs, and other milestones. Oy vey is an expression of dismay or frustration.
which hero had only one weak spot: his h: According to legend, Achilles' mother Thetis dipped him into the River Styx to grant him invulnerability, holding him by his heel. He was ultimately killed during the Trojan War when Paris struck that unprotected heel with an arrow.
which historical figure is referred to a: Stephen F. Austin brought the first 300 Anglo-American families, known as the 'Old Three Hundred', to Mexican Texas in the 1820s. Texas's state capital was named in his honor in 1839.

which holiday is known as the festival o: Diwali derives from the Sanskrit word 'deepavali', which means row of lights, and is marked by the lighting of clay lamps known as diyas. Holi is India's famous spring festival of colors.

which team has won the most stanley cups: The Montreal Canadiens hold the NHL record with 24 Stanley Cup championships, their most recent win coming in 1993, while the Toronto Maple Leafs rank second with 13 titles.
which temperature scale came first, fahr: Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit proposed his temperature scale in 1724, while Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius developed his competing centigrade scale nearly two decades later in 1742.

which term means a noncontagious inflamm: Eczema is derived from the Greek word "ekzema," which translates roughly to "boil out" or "break out." The correct spelling retains the initial "ec-" prefix.
which term means fear of spiders?: Arachnophobia comes from the Greek word "arachne," meaning spider. In contrast, xanthophobia is the fear of the color yellow, and zelophobia is the morbid fear of jealousy.
which term refers to a method of educati: Named after classical Greek philosopher Socrates, the Socratic method uses cooperative, question-and-answer dialogue to stimulate critical thinking and uncover underlying beliefs.
which term refers to dreams in which you: A lucid dream occurs when a sleeper becomes consciously aware that they are dreaming, often allowing them some degree of control over the dream's events and environment.
which term refers to the process of disp: Homogenization forces milk under high pressure through tiny valves to break down fat globules into microscopic sizes so they stay evenly suspended rather than separating into a cream layer. Pasteurization, by contrast, uses heat to kill pathogens.
which term refers to the self-defense me: Autotomy, from the Greek for self-amputation, allows animals like lizards to shed a body part to escape predators. Autonomy refers to self-governance, while apotemnophilia is a psychological disorder involving the desire to amputate a limb.
which territory is an autonomous provinc: Greenland is an autonomous constituent country within the Kingdom of Denmark, granted home rule in 1979 and expanded self-government in 2009. Iceland, though formerly under Danish rule, became a fully independent republic in 1944.
which three nations have not officially: The United States, Liberia, and Myanmar are traditionally cited as the three nations that have not fully adopted the International System of Units (SI) as their primary official measurement system.

which tunnel runs between folkestone and: The Channel Tunnel stretches 31.3 miles (50.5 km) beneath the English Channel, linking Folkestone in Kent, England, to Coquelles in Pas-de-Calais, France. It opened for regular service in 1994.
which twin towers, located in kuala lump: Standing at 1,483 feet (451.9 m), the 88-story Petronas Twin Towers held the title of the world's tallest buildings from 1998 until Taipei 101 surpassed them in 2004.
which two former u.s. presidents died on: Founding Fathers John Adams and Thomas Jefferson both passed away on July 4, 1826, exactly 50 years to the day after the adoption of the Declaration of Independence. James Monroe also died on July 4, but five years later in 1831.
which two of these are produced when an: When an acid reacts with a base in a neutralization reaction, hydrogen ions (H+) combine with hydroxide ions (OH-) to form water (H2O), while the remaining ions form an ionic salt.
which two planets of the solar system, c: Mercury and Venus are the only two planets in the solar system without natural satellites. Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, while Earth has one.

which type of cat is almost always femal: Because the gene for orange fur is carried on the X chromosome, a cat must inherit two X chromosomes to display both orange and black patches alongside white. As a result, roughly 99.9% of calico cats are female.
which type of residence hall gets its na: "Dormitory" comes from the Latin noun "dormitorium," which derives from the verb "dormire," meaning "to sleep." In medieval monasteries, it originally referred to the common sleeping quarters of the monks.
which type of rock is created by intense: Metamorphic rocks form when existing igneous, sedimentary, or older metamorphic rocks are altered by intense heat and pressure deep within the Earth. Igneous rocks form from cooling molten rock, while sedimentary rocks form from compacted sediments.
which u.s. holiday falls on the fourth t: Thanksgiving was codified by President Franklin D. Roosevelt in 1941 to permanently fall on the fourth Thursday of November. Memorial Day occurs on the last Monday of May, while Labor Day is celebrated on the first Monday of September.
which u.s. political party is also known: GOP stands for Grand Old Party, a nickname originally used in the 1870s and 1880s for the Republican Party. The party was established in 1854 primarily by anti-slavery activists.
which u.s. president declared june 14th: President Woodrow Wilson issued a proclamation officially establishing Flag Day on June 14, 1916. Congress later formalized National Flag Day with an Act of Congress in 1949.
which u.s. president died on april 4, 18: William Henry Harrison served only 31 days in office, dying from pneumonia on April 4, 1841. He was the first sitting U.S. president to die in office, which triggered the succession of Vice President John Tyler.
which u.s. president fathered 15 childre: John Tyler fathered 15 recognized children between 1815 and 1860, the most of any U.S. president. His last child, Pearl, was born when Tyler was 70 years old.
which u.s. president, the first in the n: After being shot by John Wilkes Booth at Ford's Theatre on April 14, 1865, Abraham Lincoln was carried across 10th Street to the Petersen boarding house. He died there the following morning on April 15.
which u.s. state has adopted the saguaro: Arizona designated the blossom of the saguaro cactus as its state flower in 1931. The giant saguaro cactus is native only to the Sonoran Desert in Arizona, California, and Mexico.
which u.s. state has been nicknamed the: North Carolina was dubbed the Tar Heel State because it was historically a major producer of naval stores like tar, pitch, and turpentine extracted from pine forests. The nickname gained widespread use during the American Civil War.
which u.s. state is made up entirely of: Hawaii is the only U.S. state located entirely on an archipelago, consisting of 137 volcanic islands in the Pacific Ocean. Eight main islands account for roughly 99 percent of its total land area.
which u.s. state is nicknamed the golden: California became known as the Golden State primarily due to the 1848 California Gold Rush and the golden poppy that blankets its fields in spring. The state legislature made it an official nickname in 1968.
which u.s. state was nicknamed americas: Wisconsin adopted 'America's Dairyland' on its vehicle license plates in 1940 and as an official state slogan in 1972. The state leads the nation in total cheese production, generating billions of pounds annually.
which us president delivered the followi: John F. Kennedy spoke these words during his inaugural address on January 20, 1961. The speech called for public service and civic responsibility from citizens and allies around the globe.

which us presidents face is on the 20 do: Andrew Jackson has been featured on the front of the U.S. twenty-dollar bill since 1928, when he replaced Grover Cleveland. George Washington appears on the one-dollar bill.
which us state is part of new england?: New England consists of six northeastern states: Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, and Vermont. Neighboring states like New York and Pennsylvania are part of the Mid-Atlantic region.
which van gogh painting depicts the view: Vincent van Gogh painted 'The Starry Night' in June 1889 while recovering at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence. It reflects his view from the east-facing window of his bedroom, painted just before sunrise.
which vitamin does your skin make in sun: When human skin is exposed to ultraviolet B (UVB) sunlight, it converts 7-dehydrocholesterol into previtamin D3, which then metabolizes into active vitamin D. Most other vitamins must be obtained directly through diet.
which vitamin is the orange pigment beta: Beta-carotene is a provitamin A carotenoid that the human body cleaves into retinol, the active form of vitamin A, in the small intestine. This nutrient is essential for maintaining healthy vision and immune function.
which war was fought between the norther: The American Civil War lasted from 1861 to 1865, fought between 23 northern and border Union states and 11 southern Confederate states that attempted to secede.
which war, fought in the 20th century, i: The Korean War (1950–1953) is often called The Forgotten War because it was overshadowed in American public memory by the scale of World War II and the controversy of the Vietnam War.

which was the first broadway play writte: Lorraine Hansberry's play opened on Broadway in 1959, taking its title from Langston Hughes's poem Harlem. At age 29, Hansberry also became the youngest American playwright to win the New York Drama Critics' Circle Award.
which was the first cartoon with a fully: Released in 1928, Walt Disney's Steamboat Willie made Mickey Mouse famous by synchronizing sound, voice, and musical score on film. While older cartoons used standalone audio recordings, Steamboat Willie printed the audio track directly onto the film strip.
which was the first egyptian pyramid?: Built around 2670 BC at Saqqara for Pharaoh Djoser, the Step Pyramid was designed by the architect Imhotep. It predated the smooth-sided Great Pyramid of Giza by roughly a century.
which was the first nation to adopt a me: France officially adopted the metric system in 1795 following the French Revolution to replace a chaotic patchwork of thousands of traditional regional units.
which was the first nation to become chr: King Tiridates III declared Christianity the state religion of Armenia around 301 AD after being converted by St. Gregory the Illuminator, making it the first sovereign state to do so.

which was the first sub-saharan african: Led by Kwame Nkrumah, the Gold Coast gained independence from British colonial rule on March 6, 1957, renaming itself Ghana.
which was the largest empire in pre-colu: At its peak in the early 16th century, the Inca Empire spanned roughly 2,500 miles (4,000 km) along the Andes, ruling an estimated 10 to 12 million people.
which wedding anniversary is celebrated: Dating back to the Holy Roman Empire, a husband traditionally presented his wife with a silver wreath to celebrate their 25th year of marriage.
The 60th anniversary became associated with diamonds after Queen Victoria celebrated her Diamond Jubilee in 1897, shifting the diamond milestone from the 75th year.
which wedding anniversary is known as th: Like silver for the 25th, traditional Germanic customs celebrated 50 years of marriage by presenting the wife with a golden wreath or garland.

which wizard school does harry potter at: Harry Potter attends Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in Scotland, while Durmstrang is a rival magical institute located in northern or eastern Europe.
which woodwind instrument is not made of: Modern concert flutes are edge-blown aerophones typically made of metal like silver or nickel. They belong to the woodwind family because early flutes were crafted from wood.
which word means a slum surrounding majo: The term favela originated in the late 19th century in Rio de Janeiro, named after soldiers settled on Morro da Favela, a hill covered in a shrub called favela.
which word game uses letter tiles on a 1: Invented by Alfred Mosher Butts in 1938, Scrabble is played on a 15-by-15 grid containing 225 squares with 100 letter tiles.
which word goes with the oriental symbol: In Chinese philosophy, yin and yang describe opposite but complementary forces: yin represents dark, passive, and receptive qualities, while yang represents light and active energy.
which word means a group of whales or se: A group of marine mammals such as whales, seals, or dolphins is called a pod, whereas fish gather in a school.
which word refers to a sound caused by a: Heart murmurs are abnormal rushing or whooshing sounds made by turbulent blood flow across the heart valves. While wheezing occurs in the respiratory airways, an aneurysm is an abnormal bulge in a blood vessel wall.
which word refers to the frames used to: Cels, short for celluloid sheets, are transparent plastic sheets used in traditional hand-drawn animation to layer moving characters over static backgrounds. The technique became widespread after being patented by Earl Hurd in 1914.
which word refers to the study of bones?: Osteology comes from the Greek word osteon, meaning bone, and is a subdiscipline of anatomy and anthropology. Otology is the study of the ear, while endocrinology focuses on hormones and glands.

which yankee earned the nickname mr. oct: Reggie Jackson earned the moniker Mr. October during the 1977 World Series, culminating in a three-home-run performance in Game 6 against the Los Angeles Dodgers. He batted .417 across his five career World Series appearances.

who are the presidents on mount rushmore: Sculpted by Gutzon Borglum between 1927 and 1941, Mount Rushmore features 60-foot granite heads of George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, and Abraham Lincoln. who built the famous monument taj mahal?: Mughal emperor Shah Jahan commissioned the white marble mausoleum in Agra in 1631 to honor his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal. The complex took around two decades and thousands of artisans to complete.

who created the fictional character big: George Orwell created Big Brother as the omnipresent symbol of the totalitarian regime of Oceania in his dystopian 1949 novel, 'Nineteen Eighty-Four'.

who directed the 1980 movie \"the shinin: Stanley Kubrick directed the psychological horror classic 'The Shining' (1980), which starred Jack Nicholson as Jack Torrance and Shelley Duvall as his wife Wendy.
who directed the 1985 blockbuster movie: Robert Zemeckis directed and co-wrote 'Back to the Future', with Steven Spielberg serving as an executive producer.

who headed the anglo-american invasion,: Lieutenant General Dwight D. Eisenhower served as the Commander-in-Chief of Allied Forces for Operation Torch, the successful Allied amphibious invasion of French North Africa in November 1942.
who helped theseus get out of the labyri: Princess Ariadne gave Theseus a sword and a ball of red thread to unravel as he entered the Labyrinth, allowing him to slay the Minotaur and trace his way back out.

who is known as the \"king of pop\"?: Michael Jackson earned the title 'King of Pop' following the historic global success of albums like Thriller, which remains the best-selling album of all time with estimated sales of over 70 million copies.
who is known as the \"king of rock and r: Elvis Presley became widely known as the 'King of Rock and Roll' in the mid-1950s after breakout hits like 'Heartbreak Hotel' and 'Hound Dog' catapulted the genre into mainstream pop culture.
